mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a reduction in liquidity and increased borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS > 5% and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically precedes a downturn in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which leads to a reduction in corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS declines for 3 months, or if the correlation between RSAFS decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5%, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both Housing Starts (HOUST) and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) decline simultaneously over a month, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and PAYEMS both decline in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and PAYEMS decline, or if the joint effect of these declines on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) relative to its 12-month moving average suggests strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS is above its 12-month average, or if the correlation between high PAYEMS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Industrial Production (INDPRO) is above its 6-month moving average and Real GDP (GDPC1) is below its 6-month moving average, it signals a supply-side strength coupled with demand weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO > 6mo MA and GDPC1 < 6mo MA, or if the joint effect of these conditions on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
